title: Absence of Strong Differential and Linear-Hull Effects in PRINCE
summary: The active-S-box argument yields only an average-probability result because PRINCE lacks independent round keys; it remains to prove or refute the absence of strong differential and linear-hull effects.

formal_statement.body: For full $12$-round $\mathrm{PRINCE}$, the active-S-box argument gives at least $48$ active S-boxes, with the differential probability and linear bias of each active S-box bounded by $2^{-2}$, but $\mathrm{PRINCE}$ lacks independent round keys and the resulting statement covers only average probability. Prove or refute the conjecture that, despite this round-key dependence, $\mathrm{PRINCE}$ has no strong differential effects or linear-hull effects.

scope.domain: Differential and linear cryptanalysis of the full 12-round PRINCE block cipher with its dependent round-key structure.
parameters: 48 active S-boxes — lower bound from the active-S-box argument
2^-2 — upper bound on each active S-box's differential probability and linear bias
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute that full PRINCE has no strong differential effects or linear-hull effects despite its round-key dependence.

citations.label: PRINCE - A Low-Latency Block Cipher for Pervasive Computing Applications - Extended Abstract

progress.summary: The source gives the 48-active-S-box argument and per-active-S-box bounds, then notes that non-independent round keys restrict the conclusion to average probability. It explicitly conjectures the absence of strong differential and linear-hull effects.
